annotations.text:
Four verbs where the app had three scattered popups and one it never had.

"It never happened" is the new one. Correcting a purchase refuses a quantity of nothing, so a delivery entered by mistake could only be disguised as a smaller delivery — which is what turned one wrong row into three.

"What this will change" is the guard rail: always on screen, updating as you type, so the shelf, the money and the bill are named BEFORE the save.

Pick "The figures are wrong" and attach PINV-0102 to watch it refuse.

Why it lives on Movements: a correction is about an EVENT that was recorded wrong, and the log is the only screen that shows that event in the order it happened.

Inventory answers "what is on the shelf now". Purchase invoices answers "what do I owe". Both keep one button that lands here.

One popup replaces three:

• Adjust stock → "The shelf disagrees"
• Correct the cost → "The cost is wrong"
• Correct this purchase → "The figures are wrong"

Receive more of this stays where it is — it records a new purchase, it does not correct one.
